claims.claim: The two mechanisms for heterochromatin establishment at the mat locus rely on cenH and REIII acting as nucleation centers to recruit H3K9 methyltransferase Clr4 via the RNAi machinery and the RNAi-independent ATF/CREB family proteins Atf1/Pcr1, respectively.
claims.source: These two mechanisms rely on two major cis elements cenH and REIII acting as nucleation centers to recruit the H3K9 methyltransferase Clr4 via the RNAi machinery and the RNAi-independent ATF/CREB family proteins Atf1/Pcr1, respectively (Hall et al., 2002; Jia et al., 2004a; Kim et al., 2004; Thon et al., 1999; Yamada et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: The initial nucleation and subsequent spreading of heterochromatin at the mat locus are facilitated by Swi6HP1 and HDACs (including Clr3 and Clr6).
claims.source: The initial nucleation and subsequent spreading of heterochromatin are further facilitated by Swi6HP1 and HDACs (including Clr3 and Clr6) (Jia et al., 2004a; Kim et al., 2004; Yamada et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Atf1 and Pcr1 are activated and regulated by Sty1, one of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), in response to high temperature, osmotic, oxidative, and other environmental stresses.
claims.source: As two major stress-responsive transcription factors, it has been shown that Atf1 and Pcr1 are activated and regulated by Sty1, one of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), in response to high temperature, osmotic, oxidative, and a number of other environmental stresses (Eshaghi et al., 2010; Lawrence et al., 2007; Reiter et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: The constitutive heterochromatin at centromeres is propagated stably whereas the epigenetic stability at the mat locus in vegetatively growing cells is sensitive to being continuously cultured at elevated temperatures.
claims.source: However, contrary to this pre-assumption, recent studies demonstrated that the constitutive heterochromatin at centromeres is propagated stably whereas the epigenetic stability at the mat locus in vegetatively growing cells is sensitive to being continuously cultured at elevated temperatures (Greenstein et al., 2018; Nickels et al., 2022; Oberti et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: The protein disaggregase Hsp104 is involved in buffering environmentally induced epigenetic variation at centromeres by dissolving cytoplasmic Dcr1 aggregates.
claims.source: It has been established that the protein disaggregase Hsp104 is involved in buffering environmentally induced epigenetic variation at centromeres by dissolving cytoplasmic Dcr1 aggregates (Oberti et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation to support it.

claims.claim: otr1R::ade6+ cells formed almost fully red colonies at all tested temperatures.
claims.source: Consistent with previous study (Oberti et al., 2015), otr1R::ade6+ cells formed almost fully red colonies at all tested temperatures (Figure 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B and C.

claims.claim: mat3M::ade6+ cells gave rise to variegated colonies or white colonies with low degrees of redness, or were able to grow on medium without adenine at 37°C.
claims.source: In contrast, mat3M::ade6+ cells gave rise to variegated colonies or white colonies with low degrees of redness, or even were able to grow on medium without adenine at 37°C (Figure 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B and C.

claims.claim: The mRNA levels of ade6+ increased by sevenfold in mat3M::ade6+ cells but only twofold in otr1R::ade6+ cells at 37°C compared to the same cells grown at 30°C.
claims.source: Accordingly, the mRNA levels of ade6+, as measured by quantitative RT-PCR, increased by sevenfold in mat3M::ade6+ cells but only twofold in otr1R::ade6+ cells at 37°C compared to the same cells grown at 30°C (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D.

claims.claim: When cells were grown at 37°C, H3K9me2 was reduced modestly at all heterochromatic regions.
claims.source: Our results showed that when cells were grown at 37°C, H3K9me2 was reduced modestly at all heterochromatic regions
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claims.claim: H3K9me3 enrichment was similarly reduced within cenH element-surrounding regions except pericentromeric repeats and the cenH region itself at 37°C.
claims.source: and intriguingly, H3K9me3 enrichment was similarly reduced within cenH element-surrounding regions except pericentromeric repeats and the cenH region itself (Figure 1E)
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E.

claims.claim: H3K9me3, but not H3K9me2, is a more reliable hallmark for heterochromatin.
claims.source: This is consistent with recent finding that H3K9me3, but not H3K9me2, is a more reliable hallmark for heterochromatin (Cutter DiPiazza et al., 2021; Jih et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated as supporting information with citations.

claims.claim: The RNAi mechanism is still functional and actively confers the robustness of epigenetic maintenance of heterochromatin at centromere upon heat stress.
claims.source: One previous study has revealed that the RNAi mechanism is still functional and actively confers the robustness of epigenetic maintenance of heterochromatin at centromere upon heat stress (Oberti et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation to support it.

claims.claim: At the mat locus, RNAi mechanism is required for the nucleation of heterochromatin at the cenH element and subsequent spreading across the entire mat locus, but it is dispensable for the maintenance of heterochromatin.
claims.source: At the mat locus, RNAi mechanism is similarly required for the nucleation of heterochromatin at the cenH element and subsequent spreading across the entire mat locus, but it is dispensable for the maintenance of heterochromatin (Jia et al., 2004a; Kim et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: The variegated colonies from mat3M::ade6+ cells at 37°C restored gene silencing rapidly at normal temperature 30°C after being re-plated on medium containing limited adenine.
claims.source: Indeed, in accordance with our assumption, the variegated colonies from mat3M::ade6+ cells at 37°C restored gene silencing rapidly at normal temperature 30°C after being re-plated on medium containing limited adenine (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A and B.

claims.claim: When the re-plating assay was applied to dcr1Δ, a considerable proportion of cells still emerged as variegated colonies, which was in sharp contrast to wild type cells.
claims.source: However, when this re-plating assay was applied to dcr1Δ, one of the RNAi mutants, a considerable proportion of cells still emerged as variegated colonies (designated as dcr1ΔV), which was in sharp contrast to wild type cells (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The mRNA levels of the reporter mat3M::ade6+ and cenH increased similarly and dramatically in dcr1ΔV cells compared to those in dcr1ΔR cells at both 30°C and 37°C.
claims.source: Our RT-qPCR analyses confirmed that the mRNA levels of the reporter mat3M::ade6+ and cenH increased similarly and dramatically in dcr1ΔV cells compared to those in dcr1ΔR (refers to 'red' colonies) cells at both 30°C and 37°C, whereas dg transcription was de-repressed irrespective of red or variegated colonies or temperatures (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The de-repression correlated with severe reduction in H3K9me3 levels within the entire mat locus in dcr1ΔV cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, the de-repression also correlated with severe reduction in H3K9me3 levels within the entire mat locus in dcr1ΔV cells (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Heat stress leads to defective reestablishment of stable heterochromatin at the mat locus.
claims.source: These data strongly suggested that heat stress also leads to defective reestablishment of stable heterochromatin at the mat locus.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: A composite DNA element within REIII at the mat locus contains binding sequences for Atf1/Pcr1, Deb1, and the origin recognition complex (ORC), which act together in epigenetic maintenance of heterochromatin in the absence of RNAi nucleation with Atf1 as the dominating contributor.
claims.source: It has been recently established that a composite DNA element within REIII at the mat locus contains binding sequences for Atf1/Pcr1, Deb1, and the origin recognition complex (ORC), which act together in epigenetic maintenance of heterochromatin in the absence of RNAi nucleation with Atf1 as the dominating contributor (Wang et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation to support it.

claims.claim: Extracellular stresses induce phosphorylation of Drosophila dATF-2 and mouse ATF7, two homologs of S. pombe Atf1, which provokes their release from heterochromatin and disrupts heterochromatic maintenance.
claims.source: Two previous studies showed that extracellular stresses induce phosphorylation of Drosophila dATF-2 and mouse ATF7, two homologs of S. pombe Atf1, this provokes their release from heterochromatin and thus disrupts heterochromatic maintenance (Liu et al., 2019; Seong et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Atf1 can be phosphorylated by MAPK under heat stress.
claims.source: Given that Atf1 can be phosphorylated by MAPK under heat stress (Samejima et al., 1997; Shiozaki et al., 1998)
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Atf1 abundance at the mat locus was not altered at 37°C.
claims.source: Surprisingly, ChIP-qPCR analyses showed that Atf1 abundance at the mat locus was not altered at 37°C, although it was indeed increased modestly at SPCC320.03, an euchromatic target of Atf1/Pcr1 (Eshaghi et al., 2010; Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Atf1 contains 11 putative MAPK phosphorylation sites, 10 out of them are within the first half of Atf1.
claims.source: Atf1 contains 11 putative MAPK phosphorylation sites, 10 out of them are within the first half of Atf1 (Lawrence et al., 2007; Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation and supported by Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) fully rescued the gene silencing defects observed in Psty1-HA-atf1 cells at 37°C.
claims.source: Intriguingly, cells expressing Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) fully rescued the gene silencing defects observed in Psty1-HA-atf1 cells at 37°C, which was confirmed by RT-qPCR analyses (Figure 3D and E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D and E.

claims.claim: More Atf1 was maintained at the mat locus in Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) cells compared to that in Psty1-HA-atf1 cells grown at both 30°C and 37°C.
claims.source: Consistently, more Atf1 was maintained at the mat locus in Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) cells compared to that in Psty1-HA-atf1 cells grown at both 30°C and 37°C (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3F.

claims.claim: The enrichment of H3K9me3 and heterochromatin protein Swi6HP1 at the mat locus in Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) cells was restored to the level of wild type cells.
claims.source: Moreover, ChIP-qPCR analyses showed that the enrichment of H3K9me3 and heterochromatin protein Swi6HP1 at the mat locus in Psty1-HA-atf1(10A/I) cells was also restored to the level of wild type cells (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Psty1-HA-atf1(10D/E) were almost completely unable to grow at 37°C.
claims.source: To our surprise, cells expressing Psty1-HA-atf1(10D/E) were almost completely unable to grow at 37°C (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which may be due to the toxicity caused by constitutive level of Atf1(10D/E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Patf1-atf1(10D/E) allowed cells carrying mat3M::ade6+ to be viable and form variegated or white colonies at 37°C.
claims.source: We noticed that Patf1-atf1(10D/E) allowed cells carrying mat3M::ade6+ to be viable and form variegated or white colonies at 37°C
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claims.claim: Patf1-atf1(10A/I) mat3M::ade6+ cells formed red colonies with higher degrees of redness than Patf1-atf1(WT) and Patf1-atf1(10D/E) cells.
claims.source: whereas Patf1-atf1(10A/I) mat3M::ade6+ cells formed red colonies with higher degrees of redness than Patf1-atf1(WT) and Patf1-atf1(10D/E) cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: Patf1-atf1(10D/E) visibly compromised epigenetic silencing even at 30°C.
claims.source: More strikingly, Patf1-atf1(10D/E) also visibly compromised epigenetic silencing even at 30°C (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Atf1 causes heat stress-induced defective epigenetic maintenance at the mat locus.
claims.source: Taken together, these data demonstrated that phosphorylation of Atf1 causes heat stress-induced defective epigenetic maintenance at the mat locus.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: Atf1 contributes to the epigenetic maintenance of the mat locus by actively recruiting the H3K9 methyltransferase Clr4, heterochromatin protein Swi6, and two HDACs Clr3 and Clr6.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that Atf1 contributes to the epigenetic maintenance of the mat locus by actively recruiting the H3K9 methyltransferase Clr4, heterochromatin protein Swi6, and two HDACs Clr3 and Clr6 (Jia et al., 2004a; Kim et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Atf1 from cells grown at 37°C almost completely lost its binding to Swi6HP1 but not the other three heterochromatic proteins (Clr3, Clr4, Clr6).
claims.source: We found that Atf1 from cells grown at 37°C almost completely lost its binding to Swi6HP1 but not the other three heterochromatic proteins (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Non-phosphorylatable Atf1(10A/I) from 37°C cultures remained binding to Swi6HP1 more efficiently than wild type Atf1.
claims.source: Very interestingly, non-phosphorylatable Atf1(10A/I) from 37°C cultures remained binding to Swi6HP1 more efficiently than wild type Atf1
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claims.claim: Phosphomimetic Atf1(10D/E) rendered weak binding to Swi6HP1 even when it was derived from 30°C cultures.
claims.source: and phosphomimetic Atf1(10D/E) rendered weak binding to Swi6HP1 even when it was derived from 30°C cultures (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Swi6HP1 enrichment was reduced at the mat locus, but not at pericentromeric repeats under heat stress.
claims.source: Our ChIP-qPCR analyses confirmed that Swi6HP1 enrichment was indeed reduced at the mat locus, but not at pericentromeric repeats under heat stress (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Clr3 level was slightly decreased at regions distal to the cenH nucleation center (i.e. mat2P and mat3M) but not at pericentromeres and the cenH under heat stress.
claims.source: In addition, we also noticed that Clr3 level was slightly decreased at regions distal to the cenH nucleation center (i.e. mat2P and mat3M) but not at pericentromeres and the cenH under heat stress (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Clr4 and Clr6 enrichment was not altered at all tested heterochromatin sites under heat stress.
claims.source: Consistent with our in vitro pull-down assays, Clr4 and Clr6 enrichment was not altered at all tested heterochromatin sites under heat stress (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D.

claims.claim: Atf1 and Pcr1 can form heterodimer and both are activated by MAPK in response to a variety of environmental stresses.
claims.source: It has been shown that Atf1 and Pcr1 can form heterodimer and both are activated by MAPK in response to a variety of environmental stresses (Eshaghi et al., 2010; Lawrence et al., 2007; Reiter et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Both Atf1 and Pcr1 bind to the cis elements flanking the mat3M cassette and interact with Swi6HP1 to facilitate epigenetic inheritance of heterochromatin.
claims.source: Also, both Atf1 and Pcr1 bind to the cis elements flanking the mat3M cassette and interact with Swi6HP1 to facilitate epigenetic inheritance of heterochromatin (Jia et al., 2004a; Kim et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: The binding of Pcr1 to Swi6HP1 was not affected by either heat stress or phosphorylation status of Atf1.
claims.source: In contrary to Atf1, the binding of Pcr1 to Swi6HP1 was not affected by either heat stress or phosphorylation status of Atf1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Absence of atf1 or Atf1 phospho mutants did not alter enrichment of Pcr1 at the mat locus.
claims.source: In addition, absence of atf1 or Atf1 phospho mutants did not alter enrichment of Pcr1 at the mat locus (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B)
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: Atf1 and Pcr1 respond differently and separately to heat stress in heterochromatin maintenance at the mat locus.
claims.source: These data also indicated that Atf1 and Pcr1 respond differently and separately to heat stress in heterochromatin maintenance at the mat locus.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Atf1 induced by heat stress disrupts Swi6HP1 binding affinity to Atf1 but not to Pcr1, and thus attenuates Swi6HP1 abundance at the mat locus, which consequently causes the defective maintenance of heterochromatin specifically at this site.
claims.source: Together, all these results suggested that most likely phosphorylation of Atf1 induced by heat stress disrupts Swi6HP1 binding affinity to Atf1 but not to Pcr1, and thus attenuates Swi6HP1 abundance at the mat locus, this consequently causes the defective maintenance of heterochromatin specifically at this site.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: The MAPK Sty1 is constitutively activated in wis1-DD mutant (carrying S469D and T473D mutations).
claims.source: It has been well established that the MAPK Sty1 is constitutively activated in wis1-DD mutant (carrying S469D and T473D mutations)
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information.

claims.claim: Sty1 phosphorylates and activates Atf1 in response to high temperature.
claims.source: and Sty1 phosphorylates and activates Atf1 in response to high temperature (Eshaghi et al., 2010; Lawrence et al., 2007; Reiter et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with citations to support it.

claims.claim: Cells expressing two copies, but not one copy, of wis1-DD showed severe gene silencing defects.
claims.source: Notably, cells expressing two copies, but not one copy, of wis1-DD showed severe gene silencing defects (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The mRNA levels of the kΔ::ade6+ increased dramatically in cells expressing two copies of wis1-DD.
claims.source: and consistently the mRNA levels of the kΔ::ade6+ increased dramatically in these cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The levels of both the active form of Sty1 (i.e. phosphorylated Sty1) and its downstream effector Atf1 increased in wis1-DD mutants regardless of its copy number.
claims.source: Our immunoblotting results confirmed that the levels of both the active form of Sty1 (i.e. phosphorylated Sty1) and its downstream effector Atf1 increased in wis1-DD mutants regardless of its copy number (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating constitutive activation of the Wis1/Sty1-mediated MAPK signaling.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The interaction between Atf1 and Swi6HP1 was largely disrupted in wis1-DD mutants.
claims.source: Furthermore, in vitro pull-down assays demonstrated that the interaction between Atf1 and Swi6HP1 was also largely disrupted in wis1-DD mutants (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The abundance of both H3K9me3 and Swi6HP1 bound at the mat locus but not at pericentromere decreased dramatically in cells with two copies of wis1-DD.
claims.source: Consistently, ChIP-qPCR analyses showed that the abundance of both H3K9me3 and Swi6HP1 bound at the mat locus but not at pericentromere decreased dramatically in cells with two copies of wis1-DD (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: Removal of Sty1 kinase activity by introducing either sty1 deletion mutant (sty1Δ) or ATP analogue-sensitive mutant of sty1 (sty1-T97A) into wis1-DD mutant background could relieve the negative effect of constitutive activation of MAPK Sty1 on kΔ::ade6+ reporter gene silencing, binding affinity between Atf1 and Swi6HP1 and heterochromatin stability at the mat locus.
claims.source: Intriguingly, removal of Sty1 kinase activity by introducing either sty1 deletion mutant (sty1Δ) or ATP analogue-sensitive mutant of sty1 (sty1-T97A, i.e. sty1-as2) (Zuin et al., 2010) into wis1-DD mutant background could relieve the negative effect of constitutive activation of MAPK Sty1 on kΔ::ade6+ reporter gene silencing, binding affinity between Atf1 and Swi6HP1 and heterochromatin stability at the mat locus (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Constitutive activation of MAPK signaling and resulted Atf1 phosphorylation can lead to defective epigenetic maintenance and inheritance of heterochromatin at the mat locus under normal temperatures.
claims.source: Therefore, our data lent support to the idea that constitutive activation of MAPK signaling and resulted Atf1 phosphorylation can also eventually lead to defective epigenetic maintenance and inheritance of heterochromatin at the mat locus under normal temperatures.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: A total of 11 serine or threonine residues of Atf1 were considered to be putative MAPK phosphorylation sites solely based on their fit with MAPK phosphorylation consensus S/P or T/P.
claims.source: Originally, a total of 11 serine or threonine residues of Atf1 were considered to be putative MAPK phosphorylation sites solely based on their fit with MAPK phosphorylation consensus S/P or T/P (Lawrence et al., 2007; Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation and supported by Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Mutating only the central six serine or threonine sites (S152, S172, T204, T216, S226, and T249) within Atf1 to aspartic or glutamic acid (i.e. Atf1(6D/E)) to mimic phosphorylation is as sufficient as Atf1(11D/E) and Atf1(10D/E) mutants for transcriptional activation and oxidative stress survival.
claims.source: However, one subsequent study demonstrated that mutating only the central six serine or threonine sites (S152, S172, T204, T216, S226, and T249) within Atf1 to aspartic or glutamic acid (i.e. Atf1(6D/E)) to mimic phosphorylation is as sufficient as Atf1(11D/E) and Atf1(10D/E) mutants for transcriptional activation and oxidative stress survival (Salat-Canela et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation to support it.

claims.claim: Deletion of the central domain (named as 6P domain) in Atf1 harboring six serine or threonine sites can efficiently block heterochromatin assembly capacity of Atf1 at the mat locus.
claims.source: It has also been recently shown that, similar to Atf1(11D/E) mutant, deletion of the central domain (named as 6P domain) in Atf1 harboring six serine or threonine sites can efficiently block heterochromatin assembly capacity of Atf1 at the mat locus (Fraile et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is stated as background information with a citation to support it.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of at least six residues (T77, S115, S166, S172, T204, and T249) and three other residues (S140, S152, and S226) within the central portion of Atf1 were either specifically dependent or independent on the presence of Sty1 at 37°C.
claims.source: Subsequent mass spectrometry analyses revealed that phosphorylation of at least six residues (T77, S115, S166, S172, T204, and T249) and three other residues (S140, S152, and S226) within the central portion of Atf1 were either specifically dependent or independent on the presence of Sty1 at 37°C (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Mutations of all six sites (T77, S115, S166, S172, T204, and T249) to either non-phosphorylatable alanines (Ala, A) and isoleucines (Ile, I) (i.e. Atf1(6A/I)), or phosphomimetic aspartic acids (Asp, D) and glutamic acids (Glu, E) (i.e. Atf1(6D/E)) decreased or increased the silencing and mRNA levels of mat3M::ade6+ reporter respectively, although the effect was not as strong as in Atf1(10A/I) or Atf1(10D/E) mutants.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found that mutations of all six sites to either non-phosphorylatable alanines (Ala, A) and isoleucines (Ile, I) (i.e. Atf1(6A/I)), or phosphomimetic aspartic acids (Asp, D) and glutamic acids (Glu, E) (i.e. Atf1(6D/E)) decreased or increased the silencing and mRNA levels of mat3M::ade6+ reporter respectively, although the effect was not as strong as in Atf1(10A/I) or Atf1(10D/E) mutants (Figure 6B and C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B and C.

claims.claim: Mutating four out of six these sites led to only modest effect on expression of mat3M::ade6+ at high temperature.
claims.source: We also noticed that mutating four out of six these sites led to only modest effect on expression of mat3M::ade6+ at high temperature (Figure 6B and C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B and C.

claims.claim: Atf1-S348A alone could not rescue heat stress-induced defective reporter silencing at the mating-type region.
claims.source: We found that Atf1-S348A alone could not rescue heat stress-induced defective reporter silencing at the mating-type region
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claims.claim: When Atf1-S348A was combined with Atf1(10A/I), it did not enhance the rescuing effect on heat stress-induced defective reporter silencing.
claims.source: and when it was combined with Atf1(10A/I), it did not enhance the rescuing effect on heat stress-induced defective reporter silencing (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of S348 site is not essential for regulating heterochromatin establishment and maintenance at the mating-type region.
claims.source: These results indicated that phosphorylation of S348 site is not essential for regulating heterochromatin establishment and maintenance at the mating-type region.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: Sty1 phosphorylates only some of the 11 putative MAPK phosphorylation sites in Atf1 upon heat stress.
claims.source: Overall, these data suggested that Sty1 phosphorylates only some of the 11 putative MAPK phosphorylation sites in Atf1 upon heat stress
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: Residues such as Ser140, Ser152, and Ser226 are probably phosphorylated by other kinase(s).
claims.source: and the rest of the residues, such as Ser140, Ser152, and Ser226, are probably phosphorylated by other kinase(s).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the section.

claims.claim: Cells expressing TetRoff-Swi6ΔCD but not TetRoff or Swi6ΔCD only rendered completely red colonies at 37°C.

results.result: Heterochromatic silencing at the mat locus is unstable under heat stress (37°C) compared to pericentromeres. mat3M::ade6+ cells showed variegated or white colonies and 7-fold increased ade6+ mRNA at 37°C, while otr1R::ade6+ cells remained red with only 2-fold mRNA increase. H3K9me3 was reduced at cenH-surrounding regions but maintained at pericentromeric repeats and cenH itself.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C34 provide converging evidence from multiple assays (colony color, RT-qPCR, ChIP-qPCR) demonstrating differential heat sensitivity between mat locus and pericentromeres. The data are internally consistent and supported by appropriate controls and quantification (Figure 1B-E).

results.result: Heat stress compromises reestablishment of stable heterochromatin at the mat locus. Wild-type cells rapidly restored silencing when returned to 30°C, but dcr1Δ cells maintained variegated colonies with elevated mat3M::ade6+ and cenH transcripts and reduced H3K9me3 at the mat locus.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41 demonstrate that RNAi-deficient cells cannot reestablish heterochromatin after heat stress, supported by colony assays, RT-qPCR, and ChIP-qPCR (Figure 2). The contrast between wild-type and dcr1Δ recovery provides strong evidence for the conclusion in C42.

results.result: Phosphorylation of Atf1 causes heat stress-induced defective heterochromatin maintenance at the mat locus. Non-phosphorylatable Atf1(10A/I) fully rescued silencing defects at 37°C, maintained higher Atf1 occupancy at the mat locus, and restored H3K9me3 and Swi6HP1 enrichment to wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C50 provide strong genetic evidence that preventing Atf1 phosphorylation rescues heat-induced heterochromatin defects. The data include multiple complementary assays (colony color, RT-qPCR, ChIP-qPCR) showing rescue of silencing, histone marks, and heterochromatin protein recruitment (Figure 3D-G).

results.result: Phosphorylation of Atf1 disrupts its interaction with Swi6HP1, reducing Swi6HP1 enrichment at the mat locus. In vitro pull-down assays showed Atf1 from 37°C cultures lost binding to Swi6HP1, while Atf1(10A/I) maintained binding and Atf1(10D/E) showed weak binding even at 30°C. ChIP-qPCR confirmed reduced Swi6HP1 at the mat locus but not pericentromeres under heat stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C60 provide biochemical and genomic evidence for the mechanism. The in vitro pull-down assays directly demonstrate loss of Atf1-Swi6HP1 interaction at 37°C, and phospho-mutants show expected effects. ChIP-qPCR confirms the in vivo consequence (Figure 4A-B).

results.result: Constitutive activation of MAPK signaling disrupts heterochromatin maintenance at the mat locus even at normal temperature. Cells expressing two copies of wis1-DD showed severe silencing defects, increased kΔ::ade6+ mRNA, disrupted Atf1-Swi6HP1 interaction, and decreased H3K9me3 and Swi6HP1 at the mat locus. Removing Sty1 kinase activity relieved these defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C76 provide comprehensive evidence that MAPK activation is sufficient to cause heterochromatin defects at normal temperature. The dose-dependence (two copies required), biochemical effects, and genetic rescue with sty1Δ or sty1-T97A strongly support the conclusion (Figure 5).

results.result: Mass spectrometry identified six Sty1-dependent phosphorylation sites in Atf1 (T77, S115, S166, S172, T204, T249) at 37°C. Mutating all six sites to non-phosphorylatable (6A/I) or phosphomimetic (6D/E) residues decreased or increased mat3M::ade6+ expression respectively, though less strongly than 10A/I or 10D/E mutants.
results.evaluation: Claim C81 provides direct mass spectrometry evidence for specific phosphorylation sites. Claims C82-C83 show functional validation through genetic analysis, though the weaker effect compared to 10-site mutants suggests additional sites contribute (Figure 6A-C, supplementary figures).

results.result: Tethering Swi6HP1 to the mat locus rescues heat stress-induced heterochromatin defects. Cells expressing TetRoff-Swi6ΔCD formed completely red colonies at 37°C with dramatically decreased ade6+ mRNA and restored H3K9me3 levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C90 demonstrate that artificially recruiting Swi6HP1 bypasses the Atf1 phosphorylation defect, providing strong support that reduced Swi6HP1 recruitment is the key mechanism. The tethering system is well-controlled with appropriate negative controls (Figure 7C-D).

results.result: Deletion of the anti-silencing factor Epe1 partially rescues heat stress-induced silencing defects at the mat locus. epe1Δ cells showed moderately rescued silencing and more robust H3K9me3 at 37°C compared to wild-type, mst2Δ, or leo1Δ cells. Epe1 levels at the mat locus were similar at 30°C and 37°C.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C96 show that epe1Δ specifically (not mst2Δ or leo1Δ) provides partial rescue, supported by colony assays, RT-qPCR, and ChIP-qPCR. Claim C97 indicates Epe1 is not actively recruited under heat stress, suggesting the rescue occurs through a different mechanism (Figure 8A-D).

results.result: Under heat stress, Clr3 levels decreased slightly at regions distal to cenH (mat2P and mat3M) but not at pericentromeres or cenH, while Clr4 and Clr6 enrichment was unchanged at all heterochromatin sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C62 are supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing differential effects on histone-modifying enzymes. The modest Clr3 decrease is consistent with compromised heterochromatin spreading, while maintained Clr4/Clr6 suggests the defect is not at the nucleation level (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-D).

results.result: Pcr1 binding to Swi6HP1 was not affected by heat stress or Atf1 phosphorylation status, and Pcr1 enrichment at the mat locus was unchanged in atf1Δ or Atf1 phospho-mutants, indicating Atf1 and Pcr1 respond differently to heat stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C66 demonstrate through pull-down and ChIP assays that Pcr1 behaves differently from Atf1 under heat stress. This specificity strengthens the conclusion that Atf1 phosphorylation is the key regulatory mechanism (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-B).

results.result: Endogenous expression of Atf1 phospho-mutants affects heterochromatin maintenance. Patf1-atf1(10A/I) cells formed redder colonies than wild-type at 37°C, while Patf1-atf1(10D/E) compromised silencing even at 30°C.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C54 validate the phosphorylation findings using physiological Atf1 expression levels rather than overexpression. The data support that phosphorylation status regulates heterochromatin maintenance, though the effects are more modest than with ectopic expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B).

results.result: Phosphorylation of Atf1 S438 site is not essential for regulating heterochromatin at the mat locus. Atf1-S438A alone could not rescue heat stress-induced silencing defects, and combining S438A with 10A/I did not enhance rescue.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C85 provide negative data excluding S438 as a critical regulatory site. The lack of effect when combined with 10A/I is particularly informative, though the mass spectrometry failure to detect this site limits interpretation (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).

results.result: Heat stress does not drive release of Atf1 from heterochromatin in fission yeast, unlike in Drosophila, mouse, and swine where phosphorylated ATF homologs are released. However, phosphorylation of ATF/CREB proteins by MAPK promotes heterochromatin instability in both systems.
results.evaluation: Claim C102 is supported by ChIP data (Figure 3A) showing maintained Atf1 occupancy at 37°C. Claims C103-C104 accurately contextualize the findings relative to prior work, identifying both differences (mechanism) and similarities (MAPK involvement) across species.

results.result: Background on RNAi-mediated heterochromatin establishment in fission yeast: transcripts are processed by Dcr1 into siRNAs, loaded onto Ago1 to form RITS complex, which recruits Clr4 to establish H3K9me2/3. H3K9me2/3 is bound by Swi6 and Chp2, which recruit factors like Clr3 for heterochromatin assembly.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C17 accurately summarize established knowledge about RNAi-mediated heterochromatin formation, supported by appropriate citations. This background is essential context for understanding the experimental results.

results.result: Background on heterochromatin establishment at the mat locus: two redundant pathways use cenH (RNAi-dependent) and REIII (Atf1/Pcr1-dependent) as nucleation centers to recruit Clr4. Atf1 and Pcr1 are activated by MAPK Sty1 in response to environmental stresses.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C27 accurately describe prior knowledge about mat locus heterochromatin formation and stress response pathways, supported by appropriate citations. This establishes the rationale for investigating Atf1 phosphorylation.

results.result: Prior work showed centromeric heterochromatin is stable at elevated temperatures due to Hsp104 preventing Dcr1 aggregation, while mat locus heterochromatin is temperature-sensitive.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C29 accurately cite prior work establishing the differential temperature sensitivity that motivates this study. The citations are appropriate and the knowledge claims are verifiable.

results.result: Background establishing rationale: Atf1/Pcr1 and other factors maintain heterochromatin at the mat locus in the absence of RNAi. Prior work in Drosophila and mouse showed stress-induced phosphorylation of ATF homologs disrupts heterochromatin. Atf1 can be phosphorylated by MAPK under heat stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C45 provide appropriate background from prior literature establishing the biological context and rationale for investigating Atf1 phosphorylation. The citations support the knowledge claims.

results.result: Background: Atf1 recruits Clr4, Swi6, Clr3, and Clr6 to maintain heterochromatin at the mat locus.
results.evaluation: Claim C56 accurately cites prior work establishing Atf1's role in recruiting heterochromatin factors, providing context for the mechanistic experiments.

results.result: Background: Atf1 and Pcr1 form heterodimers, are activated by MAPK in response to stress, and both bind cis elements flanking mat3M and interact with Swi6HP1.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C64 accurately cite prior work on Atf1/Pcr1 function, providing context for investigating their differential responses to heat stress.

results.result: Background: MAPK Sty1 is constitutively activated in wis1-DD mutants and phosphorylates Atf1 in response to high temperature.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C70 accurately describe the wis1-DD system and Sty1-Atf1 relationship, providing rationale for using this genetic tool to test MAPK involvement.

results.result: Background on Atf1 phosphorylation sites: 11 putative MAPK sites were identified based on S/TP motifs. Prior work showed the central six sites (S152, S172, T204, T216, S226, T249) are sufficient for transcriptional activation and stress survival, and deletion of the 6P domain blocks heterochromatin assembly.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 accurately cite prior work on Atf1 phosphorylation sites, providing context for the mass spectrometry analysis and mutant design.

results.result: Background: HDACs Sir2 and Clr3 contribute to heterochromatin spreading at the mat locus. Epe1, Mst2, and Paf1C prevent uncontrolled heterochromatin spreading.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C94 accurately cite prior work on factors regulating heterochromatin spreading, providing rationale for testing whether anti-silencing factors contribute to heat sensitivity.

results.result: Background summary: Prior studies showed pericentromeric heterochromatin is stable under heat stress due to Hsp104 buffering, while mat locus heterochromatin becomes unstable at elevated temperatures.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C101 accurately summarize prior work establishing the phenomenon investigated in this study, with appropriate citations.

results.result: Background on ATF7 in mammals: p38-dependent phosphorylation causes ATF7 release from TERRA and p16Ink4a promoters, disrupting heterochromatin and inducing senescence. TERRA can be transgenerationally transmitted. In porcine embryos, heat stress triggers p38 expression leading to ATF7 phosphorylation and blastocyst failure.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C107 accurately cite prior work on ATF7 in mammals, providing comparative context for the fission yeast findings and highlighting evolutionary conservation of MAPK-ATF regulation.

results.result: Background on mat locus function: The silent mating-type region enables mating-type switching and is crucial for efficient switching. Fission yeast employs multiple mechanisms to maintain heterochromatin at this locus, with Atf1 acting in parallel with RNAi and histone-modifying enzymes.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C112 accurately cite prior work on the biological importance of mat locus heterochromatin and the complexity of its regulation, providing context for why this locus might be particularly sensitive to environmental stress.

results.result: Background on fission yeast stress response: Spores have higher stress tolerance than vegetative cells, but fission yeast cells do not mate or undergo meiosis/sporulation above 33°C.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C114 provide biological context for the paradox that heat-sensitive heterochromatin at the mat locus prevents the stress-resistant sporulation pathway. C114 is supported by citation.

results.result: Background on heterochromatin and environmental stress: Pericentromeres and mat locus are both constitutive heterochromatin. Heterochromatin states are reversible and influenced by environmental cues. Heat stress is a prevalent trigger of epigenetic alterations affecting development in various organisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C4, C18-C23 provide general background on heterochromatin properties and heat stress effects across organisms. These are well-established concepts supported by appropriate citations where provided.

results.result: H3K9me3, but not H3K9me2, is a more reliable hallmark for heterochromatin.
results.evaluation: Claim C35 cites recent work supporting the interpretation of the H3K9me3 data. This contextualizes why the authors focus on H3K9me3 rather than H3K9me2 in their analysis.

results.result: Background on RNAi at different loci: RNAi actively maintains centromeric heterochromatin under heat stress. At the mat locus, RNAi is required for heterochromatin nucleation and spreading but is dispensable for maintenance.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C37 accurately cite prior work distinguishing RNAi requirements at different loci, providing rationale for the re-plating experiments to assess maintenance versus establishment.

results.result: Atf1 contains 11 putative MAPK phosphorylation sites, with 10 in the first half of the protein.
results.evaluation: Claim C47 accurately cites prior work and is supported by Figure 3B showing the location of these sites. This provides context for the mutant design.

results.result: Cells expressing Psty1-HA-atf1(10D/E) were almost completely unable to grow at 37°C, possibly due to toxicity from constitutive Atf1(10D/E) levels.
results.evaluation: Claim C51 reports an observation (no growth at 37°C) supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1, but the explanation (toxicity) is speculative. Alternative explanations (e.g., essential function disruption) are not excluded. The observation is valid but the mechanism is uncertain.

results.result: Residues Ser140, Ser152, and Ser226 are probably phosphorylated by other kinase(s) besides Sty1.
results.evaluation: Claim C88 is a reasonable inference from the mass spectrometry data showing these sites are phosphorylated but not Sty1-dependent. However, no direct evidence identifies the responsible kinase(s), making this speculative.
